fgetc() reads the next character from stream and returns it as an unsigned char cast to an int, or EOF on end of file or error.

getc() is equivalent to fgetc() except that it may be implemented as a macro which evaluates stream more than once.

getchar() is equivalent to getc(stdin).

getchar will give you the ascii value of a character as an int.

For the excercises, use printf to output getchar() != EOF and putchar(EOF)

ASCII Table gives a mapping from char to int.

Chars are not the same as strings, they are a single letter/number/punctuation mark in a string. If you input '2345678' in the console, the getchar() returns a single character every time it is called. So '2345678' returns 7 chars plus the EOF. The ints you would get back would be 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, and EOF in that order. If you input a string like 'ASCII' you would get 66, 83, 67, 73, 73 and EOF.
